findings.evidence: `grep -rn ofGeometricallyIntegral code/TauCeti/` → only use outside Basic.lean is Trivial.lean:65; Basic.lean:145 `(rfl)`.
findings.fix: Revert Basic.lean and define `trivial` directly as the structure literal `{ toOver := 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of K))), grpObj := inferInstance, isProper := ..., geometricallyIntegral := ... }`, keeping `@[expose]` on `trivial` alone. The local defeq the author's contest relies on is then supplied by `trivial`'s own body without widening the constructor's surface.
findings.issue: `@[expose]` is added to the general constructor `ofGeometricallyIntegral` purely so `(trivial K).toOver` reduces definitionally. This permanently exposes the body for every future consumer and contradicts `ofGeometricallyIntegral_toOver := (rfl)` (line 145), which was deliberately written to avoid downstream defeq reliance. `ofGeometricallyIntegral` has no other call site.

findings.evidence: `grep -rn trivial_toScheme code/` → no matches, despite the author's earlier reply stating it was added in 28963b3.
findings.fix: Extract it: `@[simp] lemma trivial_toScheme : (trivial K).toScheme = Spec (.of K) := (rfl)` and use it in `trivial_dim`.
findings.issue: The fact the module docstring advertises — "underlying scheme `Spec K`" (line 22) — is only a local `have h` inside `trivial_dim`. No `trivial_toScheme` exists anywhere in the repo, so any consumer wanting the underlying scheme must reprove it or unfold the exposed body.

summary: The prior two findings are fixed. Remaining: this PR newly exposes the body of the general constructor `ofGeometricallyIntegral` to serve one local defeq need, and the headline fact `(trivial K).toScheme = Spec K` is proved inline rather than stated.
